rationale_one_line: Encodes leptin secreted by adipocytes, ligand of LEPR that initiates JAK2–STAT and PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling.
Leptin receptor long isoform whose cytoplasmic tyrosines recruit JAK2, STAT3/5 and IRS proteins to trigger downstream pathways.
Tyrosine kinase pre-associated with LEPR that autophosphorylates and phosphorylates LEPR tails upon leptin binding.
Transcription factor recruited to LEPR Tyr1138 and phosphorylated by JAK2, then dimerizes to induce SOCS3 and other target genes.
Catalytic subunit p110α of class IA PI3K that generates PIP3 after binding IRS adaptors downstream of leptin.
Catalytic subunit p110β of PI3K that can sustain PIP3 and AKT activation especially when PTEN activity is low.
Serine/threonine kinase activated by PDK1 and mTORC2 that phosphorylates TSC2 to relieve its inhibition of RHEB–mTORC1.
AKT isoform dominant in metabolic tissues, phosphorylating TSC2 and FOXO1 to couple leptin/insulin signals to mTORC1 and glucose metabolism.
Catalytic subunit of mTORC1/2 that integrates leptin-driven PI3K–AKT input with nutrients to control protein synthesis and autophagy.
Scaffold subunit defining mTORC1 that recruits substrates such as S6K1 and 4E-BP1 for phosphorylation by mTOR.
Endogenous inhibitor that binds mTORC1/2 and lowers S6K1/4E-BP1 phosphorylation while relieving negative feedback to PI3K–AKT.
Stabilizing partner of TSC2 forming a GAP complex that converts RHEB-GTP to RHEB-GDP and thereby suppresses mTORC1 when active.
GAP for RHEB whose phosphorylation by AKT inactivates the TSC complex and permits RHEB-dependent mTORC1 activation.
Lysosomal small GTPase that in its GTP-bound form directly binds and activates mTORC1.
p70S6K1, canonical mTORC1 substrate phosphorylated on Thr389 that then phosphorylates ribosomal protein S6 to boost translation.
4E-BP1 translational repressor whose multisite phosphorylation by mTORC1 releases eIF4E to initiate cap-dependent translation.
40S ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylated by activated S6K1 to enhance translation of mRNAs encoding ribosomal and elongation factors.
Suppressor of cytokine signaling induced by leptin–STAT3 that binds LEPR–JAK2 and blocks further signaling as a negative feedback loop.
Insulin receptor substrate phosphorylated on tyrosines to recruit PI3K, but also on serines by S6K1 to attenuate leptin/insulin signaling.
IRS family member particularly important in hypothalamus and liver that couples leptin/insulin receptors to PI3K–AKT–mTOR activation.
Lipid phosphatase that dephosphorylates PIP3 to PIP2, directly opposing PI3K and restraining AKT–mTORC1 signaling strength.
Forkhead transcription factor phosphorylated by AKT at Thr24 leading to nuclear export and suppression of its gluconeogenic and anti-anabolic programs.

Ser/Thr kinase at the apex of the autophagy initiation complex that is directly phosphorylated by mTORC1 at Ser757 to block its activation by AMPK and suppress autophagy under nutrient-rich conditions.
ULK1 complex subunit that binds ULK1 and FIP200 and is phosphorylated by mTORC1 as well as ULK1, thereby coupling nutrient status to autophagy initiation.
FIP200 scaffold protein in the ULK1–ATG13–ATG101 complex that organizes the kinase module at phagophore formation sites downstream of mTORC1.
Master MiT/TFE transcription factor whose phosphorylation by lysosomal mTORC1 keeps it cytoplasmic; dephosphorylation allows nuclear entry to induce autophagy and lysosome genes.
TFEB paralog that is similarly controlled by mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation and drives a largely overlapping autophagy–lysosome transcriptional program.
Core scaffold of the class III PI3K (PIK3C3) complex that generates PI3P at nascent autophagosomes downstream of the ULK1 complex.
Autophagy-specific subunit of the VPS34–BECN1 complex that targets PI3P production to isolation membranes and omegasomes for autophagosome nucleation.
Class III PI3K VPS34 that produces PI3P on phagophore membranes, recruiting WIPI proteins once activated by the ULK1–BECN1–ATG14 axis.
E1-like enzyme for both ATG12 and ATG8 (LC3/GABARAP) conjugation systems, essential for LC3 lipidation and autophagosome expansion.
Forms a covalent conjugate with ATG12 that acts as an E3-like ligase to promote LC3 lipidation and autophagosome membrane elongation.
Ubiquitin-like protein conjugated to ATG5, creating the ATG12–ATG5–ATG16L1 complex required for LC3 lipidation.
Coiled-coil protein that dimerizes and tethers ATG12–ATG5 to phagophore membranes, spatially defining sites of LC3 conjugation.
Selective autophagy receptor p62 that binds polyubiquitylated cargo via its UBA domain and LC3 via its LIR motif to deliver aggregates to autophagosomes.
Late endosomal/lysosomal Rab GTPase that promotes autophagosome–lysosome fusion and proper lysosomal morphology, thereby enabling degradation of autophagic cargo.
SNARE protein recruited to completed autophagosomes that forms a STX17–SNAP47–VAMP7/8 complex to drive autophagosome–lysosome membrane fusion.
PI3P-binding effector at nascent autophagosomes that decodes the VPS34-generated PI3P signal and participates in early phagophore formation.
WIPI family member that binds PI3P and directly recruits the ATG12–ATG5–ATG16L1 complex, thereby coupling PI3K signaling to LC3 lipidation.
AMPKα1 catalytic subunit that phosphorylates ULK1 on activating sites while mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 on Ser757, together forming a regulatory triangle controlling autophagy induction.

rationale_one_line: Zinc-finger transcription factor that acts as a master repressor of autophagy and lysosome genes, functioning as a TFEB antagonist in nutrient-replete cells.
Lysosomal Ca2+ channel TRPML1 whose ROS- or nutrient-induced activation releases Ca2+ to activate calcineurin, driving TFEB dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation to enhance autophagy.

citation_short: Singh & Cuervo 2012 Int J Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: Constitutive lipid-droplet coat protein whose CMA-mediated removal or loss exposes droplets to autophagy and lipases, thereby permitting lipophagy-driven TG hydrolysis.
Perilipin family coat protein phosphorylated by mTORC1 and required for recruiting FIP200 and ATG16L1 to lipid droplets, acting as a docking platform to activate lipophagy.
Lipid-droplet protein that forms contact sites with mitochondria and FATP4 to channel lipolysis/lipophagy-derived fatty acids toward oxidative metabolism.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: Brown adipocyte lipid-droplet protein that promotes LD fusion and enlargement, increasing the size of droplets that subsequently require autophagic or lysosomal clearance.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: White adipocyte LD fusion protein (FSP27) that drives growth of unilocular droplets, limiting neutral lipase access and shaping the substrate pool for lipophagy.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: ER membrane protein that interacts with tubule-forming proteins to organize sites of nascent lipid-droplet biogenesis, thereby setting up the LD population targeted by lipophagy.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: Acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase catalyzing the final step of TAG synthesis for lipid droplet formation, affecting the amount and distribution of LD cargo available for lipophagy.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: DGAT isoform that preferentially directs TAG into cytoplasmic lipid droplets, modulating LD size and proteome in ways that influence lipophagic flux.
Adipose triglyceride lipase on LD surfaces that hydrolyzes TAG and functionally cooperates with lipophagy, with perilipin degradation enabling ATGL access.
Lysosomal acid lipase that hydrolyzes cholesteryl esters and triglycerides within lysosomes, executing the terminal lipid breakdown step after lipophagic delivery of droplets.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: Hormone-sensitive lipase that mediates cytosolic neutral lipolysis and cross-talks with lipophagy by processing droplets whose coats have been remodeled by autophagy.
ATG8 family protein LC3B that becomes lipidated on autophagosomal membranes and is specifically recruited to lipid droplets during lipophagy to mark droplet-engulfing autophagosomes.
LC3 paralog enriched on autophagosomal membranes that contributes to maturation and fusion of lipophagy-derived autophagosomes with lysosomes.
Lysosomal membrane glycoprotein essential for autolysosome formation and acid hydrolase function, required for efficient degradation of lipid droplets delivered by lipophagy.
Late endosomal/lysosomal Rab GTPase that drives movement and fusion of LD-containing autophagosomes with lysosomes in lipophagy pathways.
Fatty-acid translocase that mediates caveolae-dependent FA uptake and promotes lipid-droplet growth, thus regulating the load of lipophagy substrates in adipocytes.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: Adipocyte fatty-acid binding protein that shuttles lipolysis or lipophagy-derived fatty acids to mitochondria and other organelles for oxidation or re-esterification.
Carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A on the outer mitochondrial membrane that imports long-chain acyl-CoAs for β-oxidation, consuming fatty acids released by lipophagy.
Nuclear receptor that transcriptionally coordinates fatty-acid oxidation and autophagy, including induction of genes that promote hepatic lipophagy during fasting.

citation_short: Hara & Yoda 2019 Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Cell Biol Lipids
rationale_one_line: Patatin-like phospholipase implicated in promoting lipophagy by mobilizing lipids from droplets and providing lipid building blocks for autophagosomal membranes.

citation_short: Cao & Konrad 2012 Endocr Metab Immune Disord Drug Targets
rationale_one_line: Glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase that commits fatty acyl groups to TAG synthesis upstream of lipid droplet biogenesis.

citation_short: Olzmann & Carvalho 2019 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol
rationale_one_line: Lipid-droplet coat protein that stabilizes large neutral-lipid stores and shapes the substrate pool available for lipophagy.
Osteopontin matrix protein that binds mineral and integrins, promoting osteogenic matrix remodeling and appearing readily in calcifying VIC leading edges.
Bone sialoprotein that nucleates hydroxyapatite through its acidic and integrin-binding motifs and is a classic top-hit osteogenic marker.
Master osteogenic transcription factor that drives VIC transition into an osteoblast-like program and activates SP7, ALPL and other mineralization genes.
Tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase that hydrolyzes pyrophosphate and increases local inorganic phosphate to favor hydroxyapatite deposition.
BMP ligand that activates SMAD signaling and induces RUNX2-dependent osteogenic reprogramming in valve interstitial cells.
Late osteoblast marker osteocalcin whose expression reflects mature mineralizing programs and is often absent from top DEG lists, making it useful as a non-circular add-in.
Type I collagen alpha-1 chain that builds the osteoid-like ECM scaffold and is frequently elevated during fibrotic-to-osteogenic VIC conversion.
Type I collagen alpha-2 chain that pairs with COL1A1 to form the collagenous matrix supporting mineral deposition.
RUNX2 downstream osteogenic transcription factor Osterix that is required for maturation of osteoblast-like VICs.
BMP-responsive homeobox factor that cooperates with RUNX2 to activate osteogenic gene expression programs.
Developmental homeobox factor linked to pro-calcific reprogramming in valves and bone-forming lineages.
Osteoblast transcription factor that supports matrix protein synthesis and late-stage mineralization.
Matrix Gla protein that directly binds nascent hydroxyapatite and antagonizes BMP signaling, acting as a potent anti-calcification brake.
Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase that generates extracellular pyrophosphate, the key soluble inhibitor of mineralization.
Pyrophosphate transport regulator that exports PPi to the extracellular compartment to restrain crystal growth.
Matrix-vesicle phosphatase that produces inorganic phosphate required for hydroxyapatite nucleation.
PiT1 phosphate importer that raises intracellular phosphate and is required for phosphate-driven osteochondrogenic switching.
PiT2 phosphate transporter that regulates phosphate flux and modulates calcification susceptibility.
BMP family ligand that engages SMAD signaling and promotes osteogenic differentiation of VICs.
Canonical Wnt ligand that stabilizes beta-catenin to activate osteogenic transcription in calcifying valve cells.
Non-canonical Wnt ligand that rewires VIC signaling and supports pro-osteogenic, pro-inflammatory states.
TGF-beta ligand that drives VIC activation, ECM remodeling and pro-calcific phenotypic switching.
Wnt co-receptor that transduces canonical Wnt signals to beta-catenin during osteogenic reprogramming.
Wnt co-receptor that cooperates with LRP5 to amplify canonical Wnt signaling and mineralization.
Protective anti-osteogenic valve gene whose loss derepresses BMP2 and allows calcific reprogramming.
State-controlling transcription factor that modulates VIC quiescence versus activation and influences calcification susceptibility.
Periostin ECM protein that helps organize valve matrix and is induced during activated, remodeling VIC states.

rationale_one_line: Myeloid DAMP that signals through RAGE and TLR4 to activate NF-kB-dependent inflammatory programs.
RAGE receptor that binds S100A8/A9 and transduces NF-kB and PI3K signaling in inflammatory calcification contexts.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: Alternative receptor for S100A8/A9 that initiates MyD88-dependent inflammatory signaling.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: Adaptor recruited by TLR4 to assemble the IRAK–TRAF6 complex that activates NF-kB.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: NF-kB p50 subunit that dimerizes with RELA to drive transcription of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: NF-kB p65 subunit that mediates inflammatory gene activation downstream of RAGE/TLR4/MyD88.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: IkB alpha inhibitor that retains NF-kB in the cytoplasm until phosphorylated and degraded after receptor stimulation.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: Pro-inflammatory cytokine induced by NF-kB that amplifies the inflammatory circuit in calcifying lesions.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: Inflammasome-linked cytokine that promotes osteogenic and inflammatory activation in calcification microenvironments.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: NF-kB-responsive cytokine that engages JAK-STAT signaling and reinforces inflammatory calcification programs.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: Chemokine that recruits neutrophils and myeloid cells, sustaining inflammatory remodeling in calcified tissue.
Matrix metalloproteinase that remodels extracellular matrix and facilitates inflammatory and calcific tissue remodeling.

citation_short: Yu & Lin 2020 Signal Transduct Target Ther
rationale_one_line: Inducible nitric oxide synthase that generates reactive nitrogen species and links inflammatory signaling to oxidative stress.
Inflammasome sensor that integrates danger signals to drive caspase-1 activation and IL-1 family maturation.
Inflammasome effector protease that cleaves pro-IL-1beta and pro-IL-18 to produce active cytokines.
Inflammasome product cytokine that amplifies sterile inflammation and can contribute to calcification-associated immune activation.
